site.aiBuilds.connectTitle.context: Heading above the row of AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT…) on the public home page, introducing the steps to connect one of them to Tiledash.

site.aiBuilds.guide.context: Link under the connection steps of one AI app, to the guide that has all the steps in detail.

site.aiBuilds.howToConnect.context: Screen reader label of the steps for connecting one AI app to Tiledash, on the public home page.

params.app: The app’s name, such as Claude or ChatGPT. Not translated.

site.aiBuilds.madeAlt.context: Alt text of a picture on the public home page that shows what an AI assistant built through Tiledash, such as a widget or a floor plan.

params.kind: What kind of thing it made, a few words, already in the page’s language.

site.aiBuilds.otherApp.context: Last choice in the row of AI apps on the public home page: for an app that is not listed. MCP is a technical standard name for connecting AI apps to tools; keep it.

site.aiBuilds.otherStep1.en: Add a remote MCP server (streamable HTTP) with the address below.
site.aiBuilds.otherStep1.context: First step for connecting any other AI app to Tiledash. “The address below” is the web address shown under the steps. MCP and streamable HTTP are technical terms; keep them.

site.aiBuilds.otherStep2.en: When the app asks, sign in with your Homey account and allow it. No key to paste.
site.aiBuilds.otherStep2.context: Second step for connecting any other AI app: the app opens a login with the Homey account and asks for permission; no secret key has to be copied.

site.aiStudio.assistant.context: Title of the left panel of the animation: the AI assistant (such as Claude or ChatGPT) where the request is typed. Also its screen reader label.

site.aiStudio.calls.context: Screen reader label of the list of tool calls the AI assistant makes in Tiledash, which appear one by one in the animation.

site.aiStudio.pause.context: Screen reader label of the button that pauses the animation (moving content needs a way to stop it). A verb; the button only has an icon.

site.aiStudio.pianoAlt.context: Screen reader label of the 3D preview in the animation’s model request: the piano the assistant has put together.

site.aiStudio.play.context: Screen reader label of the button that continues the paused animation. A verb; the button only has an icon.

site.aiStudio.preview.context: Title of the right panel of the animation: the live picture of what the assistant is building.

site.aiStudio.previewOf.context: Screen reader label of the right panel: the preview of what is being built, naming the kind of request (widget, floor plan, 3D model, house in 3D).

params.request: The kind of request, such as “Widget”. Already in the page’s language.

site.aiStudio.requests.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs (Widget, Floor plan, 3D model, House in 3D) that choose which request of the animation plays.

site.aiStudio.waiting.en: The preview appears as it works.
site.aiStudio.waiting.context: Note in the empty preview panel before the assistant has done its first step: the picture shows up as the assistant works.

site.aiStudioScenes.bath.context: Name of a room drawn on the first floor in the animation’s house picture.

site.aiStudioScenes.bedroom.context: Name of a room drawn on the first floor in the animation’s house picture.

site.aiStudioScenes.firstFloor.context: Name of the upper floor in the animation’s house picture: the floor above the ground floor.

site.aiStudioScenes.groundFloor.context: Name of the lower floor in the animation’s floor plan and house pictures: the floor at street level.

site.aiStudioScenes.hall.context: Name of a room drawn in the animation’s floor plan picture: the entrance hall.

site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall1.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant reads the existing ground floor, which already has furniture.

site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall2.en: First floor: three rooms and a landing
site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall2.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds a first floor with three rooms and a landing (the open space at the top of the stairs).

site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall3.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds doors and windows to the first floor.

site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall4.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds furniture upstairs (beds, a wardrobe, a bath).

site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall5.en: The house in 3D, floor by floor
site.aiStudioScenes.houseCall5.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant opens a preview that shows the house in 3D, one floor at a time.

site.aiStudioScenes.houseLabel.context: Name of the fourth request of the animation, shown as a tab: the assistant adds a floor and shows the house in 3D.

site.aiStudioScenes.housePrompt.en: Put the first floor on top: our bedroom, the kids room and a bathroom, furnished. Show me the house in 3D.
site.aiStudioScenes.housePrompt.context: What the person types to their AI assistant: a request to add a first floor (upstairs) with a bedroom, a kids room and a bathroom, furnished, and to show the house in 3D.

site.aiStudioScenes.humidity.context: Text of the humidity line inside the pictured widget: the humidity as a percentage, such as “45 % humidity”. It is drawn inside a widget template, so it must not contain quote marks or curly brackets.

params.value: A template expression that the widget replaces by the number. Never translated or changed.

site.aiStudioScenes.kids.context: Name of a room drawn on the first floor in the animation’s house picture: a child’s room.

site.aiStudioScenes.kitchen.context: Name of a room drawn in the animation’s floor plan picture.

site.aiStudioScenes.landing.context: Name of a space drawn on the first floor in the animation’s house picture: the open space at the top of the stairs.

site.aiStudioScenes.living.context: Name of a room drawn in the animation’s floor plan picture. It also appears in the request text; use the same word as that text.

site.aiStudioScenes.modelCall1.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant draws the case (the main body) of the piano.

site.aiStudioScenes.modelCall2.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant draws the keyboard shelf and the legs of the piano.

site.aiStudioScenes.modelCall3.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds the piano keys and the music desk (the stand for sheet music).

site.aiStudioScenes.modelCall4.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant saves the finished model, with pedals, as a 3D model named like this.

site.aiStudioScenes.modelLabel.context: Name of the third request of the animation, shown as a tab: the assistant builds a 3D model of a piece of furniture.

site.aiStudioScenes.modelPrompt.en: Make our upright piano: black, 150 wide, 60 deep and 125 high, with brass pedals.
site.aiStudioScenes.modelPrompt.context: What the person types to their AI assistant: a request for a 3D model of an upright piano, with its measurements in centimetres and brass pedals.

site.aiStudioScenes.planCall1.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant starts a new floor plan draft with this name.

site.aiStudioScenes.planCall2.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds a living room of 6 by 4 metres. Keep the × sign and m for metres or use the language’s own unit abbreviation.

site.aiStudioScenes.planCall3.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds three more rooms.

site.aiStudioScenes.planCall4.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds doors and windows to the floor plan.

site.aiStudioScenes.planCall5.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant adds furniture (a sofa, a dining table, kitchen units).

site.aiStudioScenes.planLabel.context: Name of the second request of the animation, shown as a tab: the assistant draws a floor plan.

site.aiStudioScenes.planPrompt.en: Draw our ground floor: a living room of 6 by 4 metres with the kitchen next to it, a hallway and a toilet. Put in the sofa and the dining table.
site.aiStudioScenes.planPrompt.context: What the person types to their AI assistant: a request to draw the ground floor of their house as a floor plan, with furniture.

site.aiStudioScenes.toilet.context: Name of a room drawn in the animation’s floor plan picture: the toilet room.

site.aiStudioScenes.widgetCall1.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant creates a new widget with this name.

site.aiStudioScenes.widgetCall2.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant saved the widget with the temperature shown large.

site.aiStudioScenes.widgetCall3.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant saved the widget with the humidity added under the temperature.

site.aiStudioScenes.widgetCall4.en: A line of the last day
site.aiStudioScenes.widgetCall4.context: Short detail beside a tool call in the animation’s log: the assistant saved the widget with a line chart of the last day added.

site.aiStudioScenes.widgetLabel.context: Name of the first of four requests of the animation, shown as a tab: the assistant builds a widget (a tile of a dashboard).

site.aiStudioScenes.widgetPrompt.en: Make a climate tile for the kids room: the temperature big, the humidity under it and a line of the last day.
site.aiStudioScenes.widgetPrompt.context: What the person types to their AI assistant in the animation: a request for a widget that shows the temperature large, the humidity under it and a small chart of the last day.

site.asksFirst.adminTool.context: In a small code-like picture of a tool call: a grey label before the name of a tool (find_devices) that Tiledash’s own admin AI tools use. Lowercase, a few words.

site.asksFirst.afterText.en: While it runs, your sidebar says so. One tap ends it.
site.asksFirst.afterText.context: Caption under the picture of the sidebar notice: the app shows it while support can look, and one tap stops it.

site.asksFirst.allow.context: Button of the pictured question: say yes to support looking. A verb.

site.asksFirst.closedText.en: Dashboards, devices, recordings, widgets and pictures stay closed to us until you say yes.
site.asksFirst.closedText.context: Text under that title. “Us” is Tiledash support; “you” is the person using Tiledash.

site.asksFirst.closedTitle.context: Title of the first of three promises about privacy: Tiledash support can see nothing unless the person agrees.

site.asksFirst.day.context: Second choice of how long support may look, in the pictured question.

site.asksFirst.decline.context: Button of the pictured question: say no to support looking. A verb.

site.asksFirst.hour.context: First choice of how long support may look, in the pictured question.

site.asksFirst.howSupportWorks.context: Link after that paragraph, to the guide page that explains how support access works.

site.asksFirst.loggedText.en: Each question, answer and read goes in the audit log, with who and why.
site.asksFirst.loggedText.context: Text under that title. The audit log is a list the person can see of every question, answer and read, saying who did it and why.

site.asksFirst.loggedTitle.context: Title of the third promise: everything support does is recorded.

site.asksFirst.lookText.en: An access reads only the parts you allowed. Nothing in it can change your setup.

site.asksFirst.lookTitle.context: Title of the second promise: with access, support can only read, never change anything.

site.asksFirst.more.en: What we see without asking, to keep Tiledash running, is your account, your Homeys’ names and whether they’re connected.
site.asksFirst.more.context: Paragraph under the section, before two links. What Tiledash may see without asking: the account itself, the names of the Homeys (smart-home hubs) and whether they are connected.

site.asksFirst.noticeEnd.context: Small button in that sidebar notice: support can no longer look, at once. A verb.

site.asksFirst.noticeTitle.context: In a picture of the app’s sidebar: the notice shown while Tiledash support is allowed to look at the setup.

site.asksFirst.noticeUntil.context: Under that notice: when the access ends, as a weekday (abbreviated) and a time. Use the weekday abbreviation and time style of the language.

site.asksFirst.partDashboards.context: Third item of the list of what support may see.

site.asksFirst.partDevices.en: Your devices, rooms, flows and moods
site.asksFirst.partDevices.context: First item of the list of what support may see: the Homey’s devices, rooms (zones), flows (automations) and moods.

site.asksFirst.partLive.en: Values straight from your Homey, and following some of them for a while
site.asksFirst.partLive.context: Second item of the list of what support may see: live readings from the Homey, and watching some of them for a while.

site.asksFirst.privacyPolicy.context: Link after that paragraph, to the privacy policy.

site.asksFirst.questionCaption.en: The question, as Tiledash asks it.
site.asksFirst.questionCaption.context: Caption under the picture of the question the app asks.

site.asksFirst.questionFollowed.en: Values they follow are deleted when the access ends.
site.asksFirst.questionFollowed.context: Note under the list in the pictured question: readings support watched live are deleted when the access ends.

site.asksFirst.questionHomey.context: In the pictured question: which Homey it is about. Sam is a made-up person. … marks the name; keep the tags.

site.asksFirst.questionIntro.en: Jesse from Tiledash support asks to see part of your setup, to help with this:
site.asksFirst.questionIntro.context: First line of that pictured question. Jesse is a made-up person at support; the reason they give follows, quoted.

site.asksFirst.questionLength.context: Small heading in the pictured question, above the choice of how long support may look.

site.asksFirst.questionMembers.en: This includes the dashboards and floor plans Noor and Daan made on it.
site.asksFirst.questionMembers.context: In the pictured question: saying yes also lets support see what two other people (made-up: Noor and Daan) who share that Homey made on it.

site.asksFirst.questionPromise.en: They can look, not change anything. Every look is logged, and you can end it sooner.
site.asksFirst.questionPromise.context: Reassurance in the pictured question. “They” is the person at support; “every look is logged” means it is recorded in an audit log.

site.asksFirst.questionReason.en: Your front door camera shows as a motion tile, without its picture. We’d like to see how your Homey describes the doorbell.
site.asksFirst.questionReason.context: The made-up reason support gives in the pictured question, spoken by support to the user (“We” is support). A Homey is the smart-home hub.

site.asksFirst.questionSees.context: Small heading in the pictured question, above the list of what support would be allowed to see. “They” is the person at support.

site.asksFirst.questionTitle.context: Title of a picture of the window the app shows when Tiledash support asks to see part of a person’s setup.

site.asksFirst.refused.en: They haven’t allowed support to look at this.
site.asksFirst.refused.context: The answer of that admin tool in the picture when the person hasn’t said yes: a refusal. “They” is the person whose data it is.

site.asksFirst.refusedCaption.en: Our own AI tools ask first too: without your yes, they get the same no as our admin pages.
site.asksFirst.refusedCaption.context: Caption under the picture of the refused tool call: Tiledash’s own AI tools need the person’s yes as well.

site.asksFirst.step1Text.en: Who asks, the reason, and exactly which parts we would see: your devices, your dashboards, your recordings. Nothing outside them.
site.asksFirst.step1Text.context: Text under the first step’s title. Recordings are the stored history of readings.

site.asksFirst.step1Title.context: Title of the first of four steps, explaining how Tiledash support gets to look at a person’s setup: it starts with a question. “We” is Tiledash support.

site.asksFirst.step2Text.en: No is a fine answer. Or yes, for 1 hour, 1 day or 7 days. A question you leave runs out after a week.
site.asksFirst.step2Text.context: Text under the second step’s title. An unanswered question expires by itself after a week.

site.asksFirst.step2Title.en: You decide, and for how long
site.asksFirst.step2Title.context: Title of the second step: the person answers, and chooses how long support may look.

site.asksFirst.step3Text.en: Your sidebar says support can look, with End right there. We can look, never change, and every look goes in the audit log.
site.asksFirst.step3Text.context: Text under the third step’s title. “End” is the name of a button in the app’s sidebar that stops the access at once; the audit log is a list of everything support did.

site.asksFirst.step3Title.en: You see it while it runs
site.asksFirst.step3Title.context: Title of the third step: while support can look, the person sees it in the app.

site.asksFirst.step4Text.en: It ends by itself. Values we followed for a while are deleted with it. Before your yes and after, our admin pages and tools are closed.
site.asksFirst.step4Text.context: Text under the fourth step’s title. “Values we followed” are readings support watched live during the access.

site.asksFirst.step4Title.context: Title of the fourth step: the access ends by itself.

site.asksFirst.week.context: Third choice of how long support may look, in the pictured question.

site.contactForm.addressUse.en: We use your address only to answer you.
site.contactForm.addressUse.context: Small note beside the send button of the contact form, before a link to the privacy statement: the e-mail address is used only to reply. “We” is the Tiledash team.

site.contactForm.another.context: Link-like button under the confirmation: opens the empty contact form again to write another message.

site.contactForm.answerAt.context: Line under that confirmation: the answer will be sent to the e-mail address the person entered. “We” is the Tiledash team.

params.email: The e-mail address the person typed. Not translated.

site.contactForm.busy.en: That’s a lot of messages from here; try again in a while.
site.contactForm.busy.context: Error under the contact form when too many messages were sent from the visitor’s address in a short time.

site.contactForm.email.context: Label of the e-mail address field of the contact form.

site.contactForm.emailError.en: Enter the e-mail address we can answer you on.
site.contactForm.emailError.context: Error under the e-mail field of the contact form when it is empty or not an e-mail address. “We” is the Tiledash team.

site.contactForm.failed.en: It didn’t go out. Check your connection and send it again.
site.contactForm.failed.context: Error under the contact form when sending the message failed, for example because the connection broke.

site.contactForm.message.context: Label of the message field (a large text box) of the contact form.

site.contactForm.messageError.en: Tell us a little more first.
site.contactForm.messageError.context: Error under the message field of the contact form when the message is too short (under about ten characters).

site.contactForm.messagePlaceholder.en: A question, something that broke or an idea
site.contactForm.messagePlaceholder.context: Grey example text inside the empty message field of the contact form: what people can write about.

site.contactForm.name.context: Label of the name field of the contact form. A short label; the field is optional.

site.contactForm.optional.context: Small note after the name field’s label, saying the field can be left empty. Keep the brackets.

site.contactForm.privacy.context: Link after that note, to the privacy statement.

site.contactForm.send.context: Button that sends the contact form. A verb.

site.contactForm.sending.context: Text of the contact form’s send button while the message is being sent.

site.contactForm.thanks.context: Heading of the confirmation shown after the contact form was sent.

site.contactForm.unavailable.en: Messages can’t be sent from the site right now; try again later.
site.contactForm.unavailable.context: Error under the contact form when sending messages is switched off or down at the moment.

site.ctaBand.login.context: Button in that closing band, on the plan cards and on the home page’s first screen: it goes to the Tiledash app, where you log in with your Homey account. Homey is a product name.

site.ctaBand.text.en: Log in with your Homey account, pick the dashboards you want and watch them fill in. It takes a couple of minutes.
site.ctaBand.text.context: Text of that closing band, under its heading: logging in with the Homey account (Homey is the smart-home hub) and getting dashboards takes a few minutes.

site.ctaBand.title.en: Put your home on a screen tonight.
site.ctaBand.title.context: Heading of the closing band at the bottom of a public site page, inviting the visitor to start. A friendly, short sentence.

site.docs.currentFallback.context: Label of the folded menu above a docs page on a phone, when the page isn’t in the menu; normally it shows the page’s own name. The name of the documentation section.

site.docs.homeLead.en: Find what you want to do, or search for it.
site.docs.homeLead.context: The line under the heading of the docs’ first page, above the search box and the list of things people come to do.

site.docs.homeTasks.context: Heading of a list on the docs’ first page: each entry is something a visitor wants to do (“Build a dashboard”) and links to the page for it, so it must read as the start of a sentence the entries complete.

site.docs.homeTitle.context: Heading of the docs’ first page on the public site, above the search box. Tiledash is the product name and stays.

site.docs.navLabel.context: Screen reader label of the docs’ side menu on the public site (the list of pages on the left of every docs page). The name of the documentation section.

site.docs.next.context: Small label above the title of the page after this one, in the links under a docs or features page. A right arrow stands beside it.

site.docs.pagerLabel.context: Screen reader label of the two links under a docs or features page that lead to the page before and the page after it.

site.docs.previous.context: Small label above the title of the page before this one, in the links under a docs or features page. A left arrow stands beside it.

site.docs.tocLabel.context: Small heading above the list of a docs page’s sections, beside the text on wide screens; also its screen reader label. Each entry jumps to a section of the page being read.

site.ecosystem.ai.en: Or let the assistant you already use build it: Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or Cursor make your widgets and 3D models and check them in a live preview.
site.ecosystem.ai.context: Sentence on the public home page, followed by a “Pro” badge: an AI assistant can build widgets and 3D models for the person. Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and Cursor are product names.

site.ecosystem.howItWorks.context: Link after that sentence, to the guide page about using an AI assistant with Tiledash.

site.ecosystem.live.context: Caption under the tile in the picture of the widget editor: the tile is drawn live with the values of the person’s own devices.

site.ecosystem.modelsText.en: Scan your sofa with your phone, or let your AI build one, for your floor plans.
site.ecosystem.modelsText.context: Text under that title: a 3D model of a piece of furniture can be scanned with a phone, or built by the person’s AI assistant.

site.ecosystem.modelsTitle.context: Title of the third kind of thing people make: 3D furniture for floor plans.

site.ecosystem.noProblems.context: Status in the picture of the widget editor: the template has been checked against every demo device and no problem was found.

site.ecosystem.partialsText.en: Building blocks your widgets share, with typed settings.
site.ecosystem.partialsText.context: Text under that title. “Typed settings” are settings with a declared type (number, text…).

site.ecosystem.partialsTitle.context: Title of the second kind of thing people make: a partial is a building block that several widgets share.

site.ecosystem.step1Text.en: Every save kept, with its changes.
site.ecosystem.step1Text.context: Text under that step: every time you save, the version is kept, and you can see what changed.

site.ecosystem.step1Title.context: Title of the first of four steps in how something you made travels to other people. The Workshop is the part of the app where you make your own widgets, themes and models.

site.ecosystem.step2Text.en: Free, from the app or the command line.
site.ecosystem.step2Text.context: Text under that step: publishing costs nothing, and works from the app or a terminal.

site.ecosystem.step2Title.context: Title of the second step: you publish it to the Community, where people share things they made.

site.ecosystem.step3Text.en: Previewed on their own devices first.
site.ecosystem.step3Text.context: Text under that step: before installing, people see it drawn with their own devices’ values.

site.ecosystem.step3Title.context: Title of the third step: other people install what you published.

site.ecosystem.step4Text.en: They choose when, and can go back.
site.ecosystem.step4Text.context: Text under that step: the people who installed it decide when to update and can return to the old version.

site.ecosystem.step4Title.context: Title of the fourth step: when you publish a new version, installers can get it.

site.ecosystem.tabSettings.context: Tab name in a picture of the widget editor: the tab where a widget’s settings are declared.

site.ecosystem.tabStyle.context: Tab name in a picture of the widget editor: the tab with the widget’s CSS (its looks).

site.ecosystem.tabTemplate.context: Tab name in a picture of the widget editor on the public home page: the tab with the widget’s HTML and template code.

site.ecosystem.themesText.en: Your colours, gradients, fonts, corners and glow, and CSS for the rest.
site.ecosystem.themesText.context: Text under that title. CSS is the language for styling web pages; keep the name.

site.ecosystem.themesTitle.context: Title of the fourth kind of thing people make: a theme sets the colours, fonts and corners of a dashboard. It is a Pro feature (a badge follows).

site.ecosystem.widgetsText.en: HTML and Liquid, drawn live against your own devices as you type.
site.ecosystem.widgetsText.context: Text under that title. HTML and Liquid (a template language) are names; keep them.

site.ecosystem.widgetsTitle.context: Title of the first of four kinds of things people make in Tiledash (widgets, partials, 3D models, themes). A widget is a tile on a dashboard.

site.energyHouse.badge.context: Small badge on the photo of the Energy house: it is a new feature.

site.energyHouse.foundText.en: It reads your energy meters: solar on the roof, the grid, the home battery and the car. What your home doesn’t have isn’t in the picture.
site.energyHouse.foundText.context: Text under that title: the Energy house shows only the parts the home really has.

site.energyHouse.foundTitle.context: Title of the first of three points about the Energy house: it finds the person’s energy devices by itself.

site.energyHouse.photoAlt.en: A tablet on a sideboard beside two vases, showing the Energy house: 175 W from the battery, 895 W used in the house and 720 W from the grid, with temperatures pointed out around the house
site.energyHouse.photoAlt.context: Alt text of a photo of a tablet on a sideboard that shows the Energy house screen. W is watts (keep the unit).

site.energyHouse.powerText.en: Each value sits on its part of the house and moves with your home: what the panels make, what the car takes, what goes back to the grid.
site.energyHouse.powerText.context: Text under that title: values (what the solar panels produce, what the car charger uses, what is returned to the grid) move live.

site.energyHouse.powerTitle.context: Title of the second point: live power values are drawn on the picture of the house.

site.energyHouse.readingsText.en: Point any reading at a place of the house: the hot water upstairs, the heat pump, a phase at the meter cupboard, outside by the tree.
site.energyHouse.readingsText.context: Text under that title: examples of readings (temperatures, a phase of the electricity meter) placed at their spot in the house.

site.energyHouse.readingsTitle.context: Title of the third point: any reading can be placed on a spot of the house picture.

site.energyHouse.tutorial.en: Set one up in four minutes
site.energyHouse.tutorial.context: Link to the tutorial that sets up an Energy house; it takes about four minutes.

site.features.allFeatures.context: First entry of the features section’s menu: opens the overview of every feature. Also the name shown for that overview in the folded phone menu and in the page-before link under the first feature.

site.features.allText.en: Flows, Logic variables, moods and every device, with tap, hold and double tap.
site.features.allText.context: Text under that title. Flows (automations), Logic variables and moods are Homey’s own names for its features; keep them as Homey’s app names them. Tap, hold and double tap are touch gestures.

site.features.allTitle.context: Title of a tile in the public home page’s grid of six features: everything Homey has can be on a dashboard.

site.features.energyText.en: Solar, battery, grid and car, moving as it happens, and the cheapest hours ahead.
site.features.energyText.context: Text under that title: live flows of solar power, home battery, the grid and an electric car, and the hours with the lowest electricity price.

site.features.energyTitle.context: Title of a tile in the public home page’s grid of six features: energy flows (solar, battery, grid, car) shown live.

site.features.historyText.en: Days, months or years of any reading in a chart, kept for as long as your plan says.
site.features.historyText.context: Text under that title: charts of any reading over days, months or years. “Your plan” is the Free or Pro plan, which sets how long history is kept.

site.features.historyTitle.context: Title of a tile in the public home page’s grid of six features: you pick which readings are recorded and shown in charts.

site.features.homeyText.en: On your own dashboards, live values and taps go from your screen to your Homey, not through us.

site.page.reference.settings.context: Heading on the Style variables page of the template reference, above the explanation that a widget’s settings are available as CSS variables. Also an entry of the page’s table of contents.

site.page.reference.tapsMark.context: Column heading of a table on the Actions page: the attribute (code) a widget puts on an element.

site.page.reference.tapsWhat.context: Column heading of a table on the Actions page: what the mark in the same row does.

site.page.reference.tileLayout.context: Heading on the Style variables page of the template reference, above a table of the CSS variables that tell a widget’s style how its tile is laid out. Also an entry of the page’s table of contents.

site.page.reference.tileLayoutIntro.en: Set by the tile’s alignment in the Style panel; read them to place your content.

Apart from the Device widget, which is built in, they are Tiledash’s own in the <link>Community</link>: every account has them without installing, and they get better without waiting for an app update.

site.planPoints.freeFloorPlan.en: A live floor plan of your house
site.planPoints.freeFloorPlan.context: Bullet point on the Free plan card: a floor plan of the house that shows live states.

site.planPoints.freeOwn.en: Make your own widgets and share them
site.planPoints.freeOwn.context: Bullet point on the Free plan card: people can make their own widgets and share them with others.

site.planPoints.freeScreens.en: A paired kitchen tablet and a link for a guest
site.planPoints.freeScreens.context: Bullet point on the Free plan card: one tablet can be paired with a code, and a share link can be given to a guest.

site.planPoints.freeWidgets.en: Every widget, on every screen you own
site.planPoints.freeWidgets.context: Bullet point on the Free plan card: all widgets are included, on all of the person’s screens.

params.readings: The number of readings that can be recorded.

params.homeys: The number of Homeys, such as “One Homey”. Not translated.

site.planPoints.proHistory.en: Years of history, and your old Homey Insights
site.planPoints.proHistory.context: Bullet point on the Pro plan card: history is kept for years, and the old readings from Homey Insights (Homey’s own history feature; a name) can be imported.

site.planPoints.proLimits.context: Bullet point on the Pro plan card: how many Homeys and dashboards it has, and that the number of screens has no limit, such as “Three Homeys, 50 dashboards, screens without limits”.

params.dashboards: The number of dashboards, such as “50 dashboards”. Not translated.

site.planPoints.proThemes.en: Your own themes and living wallpapers
site.planPoints.proThemes.context: Bullet point on the Pro plan card: own themes (colours, fonts) and living wallpapers (animated backgrounds such as weather).

site.pricingCards.atCheckout.en: Monthly or yearly, price at checkout
site.pricingCards.atCheckout.context: Price line on the Pro plan card when the prices could not be read: Pro is paid per month or per year, and the price shows when paying.

site.pricingCards.compare.context: Button on the Pro plan card: it goes to the table that compares Free and Pro line by line.

site.pricingCards.freePledge.en: No trial. No timer. No card.
site.pricingCards.freePledge.context: Short pledge on the Free plan card: there is no trial period, no countdown and no payment card needed. Three very short sentences.

site.pricingCards.freePrice.context: Price line on the Free plan card: it costs nothing, for good (forever). … marks the amount; keep the tags.

site.pricingCards.freeSay.en: Free stays free. Nothing turns into a bill after 14 days, or ever: you only pay when you pick Pro yourself.
site.pricingCards.freeSay.context: Paragraph on the Free plan card: the Free plan never becomes a paid one by itself; paying only starts when the person chooses the Pro plan.

site.pricingCards.perMonth.context: Price line on the Pro plan card when the price is per month, such as “€4 a month”. … marks the amount; keep the tags.

params.price: The amount with its currency, such as “€4”. Not translated.

site.pricingCards.perYear.context: Price line on the Pro plan card when only a yearly price is known, such as “€40 a year”. … marks the amount; keep the tags.

params.price: The amount with its currency, such as “€40”. Not translated.

site.pricingCards.perYearPlain.context: The yearly price of Pro as the other way to pay, shown after the monthly one and a dot, such as “€40 a year”.

params.price: The amount with its currency, such as “€40”. Not translated.

site.pricingCards.proPledge.context: Short pledge on the Pro plan card: Pro is only for when the person wants it.

site.pricingCards.proSay.en: Everything in Free, plus the things that cost us to run. Cancel any time; going back to Free never deletes a thing.
site.pricingCards.proSay.context: Paragraph on the Pro plan card. Pro includes everything in Free, plus features that cost Tiledash money to run (AI, history, 3D). “Us” is Tiledash. Going back to Free deletes nothing.

site.pricingTable.caption.context: Screen reader caption of the table that compares the Free and the Pro plan line by line. Free and Pro are plan names and stay.

site.pricingTable.noteIncludingVat.en: Prices include VAT. Pay monthly or yearly with PayPal, and cancel any time. Going back to Free never deletes your dashboards.
site.pricingTable.noteIncludingVat.context: Note under the plans table: the prices include VAT (value added tax), payment is with PayPal per month or year, and ending Pro deletes nothing. PayPal is a product name.

site.pricingTable.noteNoPrices.en: Pro is paid monthly or yearly; you see the price at checkout, with VAT where it applies. Going back to Free never deletes your dashboards.
site.pricingTable.noteNoPrices.context: Note under the plans table when the prices could not be read: Pro is paid per month or year, and the price (with VAT where it applies) shows when paying.

site.pricingTable.notePlusVat.en: Plus VAT where it applies. Pay monthly or yearly with PayPal, and cancel any time. Going back to Free never deletes your dashboards.
site.pricingTable.notePlusVat.context: Note under the plans table: VAT (value added tax) is added to the prices where it applies, payment is with PayPal per month or year, and ending Pro deletes nothing. PayPal is a product name.

site.reference.attribute.context: Column heading of the table of a component in the template reference: its attributes, the names written in the opening tag.

site.reference.defaultIs.context: Start of a note in the template reference after the description of an attribute, followed by the value it has when left out as code and a full stop: “Default center.”. Only the word before the value.

site.reference.takes.context: Column heading of the table of a filter, function or action in the template reference: what it takes in (its arguments).

site.reference.whatItIs.context: Column heading in the template reference tables: the description of each attribute or argument.

site.roadmap.everything.context: Link under that list, to the changelog page that lists every release and all its changes.

site.roadmap.missing.en: Missing something? Plans change with what people ask for.
site.roadmap.missing.context: Line at the bottom of the roadmap page, before a link: invites people to say what they miss; the plans follow what people ask for.

site.roadmap.share.context: Link after that line, to the ideas channel on Tiledash’s Discord. Discord is a product name.

site.roadmap.shipped.context: Heading on the public roadmap page above the list of features that were released lately.

site.search.empty.en: Nothing matches “{query}”. Try a widget’s name, a filter or a setting.

site.sections.copy.context: Button on every code block in the docs: copies the code to the clipboard.

site.widgetDocs.listAnd.context: Joins a list of names in a sentence: the first ones are already joined with commas, as in “Humidity, CO₂ and Battery”.

params.items: The first names, joined with commas.

site.widgetDocs.listOr.context: Joins a list of actions in a sentence: the first ones are already joined with commas, as in “open the device, start a flow or set a mood”.

params.items: The first items, joined with commas.

site.widgetDocs.maxLength.context: How long the text of a text option may be, like “Up to 20 characters”.

params.count: The number of characters, a whole number.

site.widgetDocs.off.context: The value of a switch setting that is off, shown as its default and as a caption under a preview of a tile with the switch off; also the caption of a device that is off.

site.widgetDocs.on.context: The value of a switch setting that is on, shown as its default and as a caption under a preview of a tile with the switch on; also the caption of a device that is on.

site.widgetDocs.percent.context: The default of a percentage option, like “50 %”. Keep the spacing the language uses before the percent sign.

params.percent: The number, a whole number, not translated.

site.widgetDocs.quoted.context: The default of a text option, in quotation marks, like “Kitchen”. Use the language’s own quotation marks.

site.widgetDocs.range.context: The range of a number option, like “1 h to 8 h”.

params.max: The largest value with its unit, not translated.
params.min: The smallest value with its unit, not translated.

site.widgetDocs.sentenceAll.en: What tapping, holding and tapping {part} twice do. Each can {actions}. Until you choose, {tap}, {hold} and {double}.
site.widgetDocs.sentenceAll.context: Description of a tile’s tap setting on a widget’s page: one setting for a tap, a hold and a double tap. {tap}, {hold} and {double} are short clauses (“a tap does nothing”, “holding it will open the device”).

params.actions: The list of what each gesture can do, like “switch the device on or off, open the device or start a flow”.
params.double: Clause about what a double tap does by default.
params.hold: Clause about what a hold does by default.
params.part: What is tapped, like “the tile” or “Temperature”: the name of a part of the widget, lower case when it starts with “The”.
params.tap: Clause about what a tap does by default.

site.widgetDocs.sentenceHold.en: What holding {part} does. It can {actions}. Until you choose, {outcome}.
site.widgetDocs.sentenceHold.context: Description of a tile’s hold setting on a widget’s page: a setting for the hold gesture alone.

params.actions: The list of what a hold can do, like “open the device or start a flow”.
params.outcome: Clause about what a hold does by default, like “it does nothing” or “it will open the device”.
params.part: What is held, like “the tile” or “Temperature”: the name of a part of the widget.

site.widgetDocs.sizeLarge.context: Default value of a size option, shown as “Default: Large”. One of small, medium and large.

site.widgetDocs.sizeMedium.context: Default value of a size option, shown as “Default: Medium”. One of small, medium and large.

site.widgetDocs.sizeSmall.context: Default value of a size option, shown as “Default: Small”. One of small, medium and large.

site.widgetDocs.unavailable.context: Caption under a preview of a tile as it looks when its device cannot be reached.

site.widgetGallery.builtIn.context: Small badge beside a widget’s name in the widget gallery of the public site: this widget is part of the app itself instead of being installed from the Community.

site.widgetPage.choiceLabel.context: Screen reader description of a picture of a widget’s tile with one choice of an option made.

site.widgetPage.communityNote.en: Tiledash’s own, as {id}. It’s in every account’s widget picker, nothing to install, and gets better by itself. About the community
site.widgetPage.communityNote.context: Note under the name of a widget on its page, after the badge “Official, in the community”: the widget is published by Tiledash in the Community, comes with every account and is updated without an app update. <code> wraps the widget’s id, <link> is a link to the page about the Community.

params.id: The widget’s id in the Community, like @tiledash/climate. Not translated.

site.widgetPage.communitySeal.context: Small badge at the start of a note under the name of a widget that Tiledash itself publishes in the Community (the shared library of widgets): it is an official one.

site.widgetPage.crumbWidgets.context: First part of the breadcrumb above a widget’s name on its page of the public site: a link back to the list of all widgets.

site.widgetPage.defaultBadge.context: Small badge beside a choice (or On / Off) under an option on a widget’s page: this is the choice the option has until the user changes it.

site.widgetPage.defaultValue.context: Small grey note under an option’s description on a widget’s page: the value the option has until the user changes it.

params.value: The default value, like “3 h”, “On” or “Small”.

site.widgetPage.factAlsoShows.context: Label of a fact at the top of a widget’s page: the extra readings the widget shows when the device has them (“Humidity, CO₂ and Battery”).

site.widgetPage.factFits.context: Label of a fact at the top of a widget’s page: which devices the widget can show (“Any device with temperature”).

site.widgetPage.factSize.context: Label of a fact at the top of a widget’s page: how big the tile is by default and how small and large it can be.

site.widgetPage.fitsAnyDashboard.en: Any dashboard: it isn’t tied to one device
site.widgetPage.fitsAnyDashboard.context: Which dashboards a widget fits when it shows no single device (a clock, electricity prices).

site.widgetPage.fitsAnyDevice.context: Which devices a widget fits when it is not limited to one kind of device; followed by what the device needs (“Any device with temperature”).

site.widgetPage.fitsDevice.context: Which devices a widget fits, like “Light with turned on” or “Any device with temperature”: the kinds of device, then what the device must be able to do.

params.fits: The kinds of device, like “Light” or “Any device”.
params.needs: The readings the device needs, in lower case, like “temperature”.

site.widgetPage.heroLabel.en: {title}, as it looks on a dashboard
site.widgetPage.heroLabel.context: Screen reader description of the picture of a widget’s tile at the top of its page.

site.widgetPage.optionsHeading.context: Heading of the list of a widget’s options (its settings) on its page of the public site.

site.widgetPage.optionsHint.en: Change these in the tile’s settings: <configure>Configure…</configure> on the tile in edit mode.
site.widgetPage.optionsHint.context: Hint under the heading “Options” on a widget’s page: where in the app the options are changed. <configure> wraps the name of the “Configure…” button as the app shows it, and is shown in bold.

site.widgetPage.showcaseLabel.context: Screen reader label of the section on a widget’s page that shows the widget’s tile with an introduction.

site.widgetPage.sizeFacts.context: The size of a widget in tiles at the top of its page, like “3 × 2 tiles, from 1 × 0.5 to 6 × 4”: columns × rows.

params.byDefault: Its default size, like “3 × 2”. Not translated.
params.largest: Its largest size, like “6 × 4”. Not translated.
params.smallest: Its smallest size, like “1 × 0.5”. Not translated.

site.widgetPage.stateLabel.context: Screen reader description of a picture of a widget’s tile as it looks with its device on, off or unavailable.

params.state: The state in lower case: on, off or unavailable.
params.title: The widget’s name.

site.widgetPage.statesHeading.context: Heading above three pictures of a widget’s tile: with its device on, off and out of reach (“away” means the device cannot be reached).

site.widgetPage.switchOffLabel.context: Screen reader description of a picture of a widget’s tile with a switch option turned off.

site.widgetPage.switchOnLabel.context: Screen reader description of a picture of a widget’s tile with a switch option turned on.

site.widgetPreview.label.context: Screen reader label of a picture of a widget (a tile of a dashboard) in the widget gallery and docs of the public site, such as “Clock widget”.

params.widget: The widget’s name, such as “Clock”. Not translated here.
